 GILLIBRAND, MERKLEY INTRODUCE LEGISLATION TO ADDRESS REPUBLICAN CUTS AND HELP STUDENTS ACCESS ESSENTIAL GRADUATE DEGREES
 November 17, 2026 
 Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senators Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) and Jeff Merkley (D-OR) introduced the Professional Student Degree Act to ensure financial stability for students and strengthen essential workforce pipelines. The bill would reverse harmful Republican cuts to federal student loan programs by expanding the definition of a “professional degree” to include certain critical graduate programs currently excluded by the U.S. Department of Education (ED), such as those in nursing, education, and public health.
 Currently, ED’s implementation of federal student loan provisions enacted by President Trump and congressional Republicans under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act creates an immediate “loan cliff” for certain graduate degrees. By narrowing the definition of a “professional degree” to just 11 eligible programs, the current framework severely limits financial access to graduate programs in essential fields already facing critical labor shortages. 
 Students in these newly designated “non-professional” programs face annual student loan caps that are almost $30,000 lower, and aggregate limits $100,000 lower, than students in designated professional tracks. This limits students’ ability to secure the federal loans needed to complete their education and threatens to worsen nationwide workforce shortages, particularly in healthcare.
 The Professional Student Degree Act would correct this by adding several key graduate programs to the federal list of professional degrees eligible for higher borrowing limits. 
 “Students who want to pursue critical fields like social work, public health, nursing, and education should not have to break the bank to serve their communities,” said Senator Gillibrand. “This bill would expand the definition of what constitutes a professional degree, giving students in high-need fields access to the financial resources they need to complete their education and serve others. This bill would help our students, our universities, and our communities, and I’m determined to get it passed.” 
 “Nurses, teachers, and social workers are dedicated public servants, and Congress must do everything it can to help recruit the next generation of these heroes,” said Senator Merkley. “We’re already facing a shortage of these critical workers, and new limits on federal student loans for these professions and others threaten to further jeopardize the future of our workforce. Financial freedom and flexibility are essential to aspiring students, and I’m leading the charge with my colleagues to oppose these dangerous changes and stand up for affordable student loans so folks can continue to achieve their dreams and serve the public.” 
 The Professional Student Degree Act would impact the following degree programs:
 Maintains Professional Status for: Pharmacy, Dentistry, Veterinary Medicine, Chiropractic, Law, Medicine, Optometry, Osteopathic Medicine, Podiatric Medicine, Theology, Clinical Psychology
 Restores and Codifies Professional Status for: Social Work, Audiology, Physician Assistant, Occupational Therapy, Physical Therapy, Nursing, Public Health, Business Administration and Management, Accounting, Architecture, Education, and Special Education
 Flexibility to Expand: The Secretary of Education may add any other programs that meet “professional degree” requirements.
 Without a statutory or legislative fix, students entering these costly but essential degree programs will be priced out of the workforce, further destabilizing already high-need professions.
 The bill has been endorsed by the American Academy of Audiology, American Academy of Physician Associate, American Association of State Colleges and Universities, American Council on Education, American Institute of Architects, American Institute of Architecture Students, American Physical Therapy Association, Association of Collegiate Schools of Architecture, Association of Public and Land-grant Universities, Columbia University, Commission on Independent Colleges & Universities, Dominican University New York, National Architectural Accrediting Board, National Council of Architectural Registration Boards, National Organization of Minority Architects, New York Medical College, Oncology Nursing Society (ONS), Physician Assistant Education Association, Yale University, Binghamton University, and the University at Buffalo.
 The full text of the Professional Student Degree Act can be found here .
